title: Foreign P&ID: instrument index, line list, equipment list
summary: Open a P&ID somebody else drew, read its connectivity graph with a confidence per node, and write the instrument index, the line list and the equipment list as CSV, without modifying the drawing.

notes: A foreign drawing's nodes come from block names and TAG attributes (confidence 0.6) or from geometry alone (0.3): read graph.stats.confidence_min before trusting a list, and never present a heuristic row as catalogued.
The three lists read the drawing; only their CSV files are written. The revision checks prove the drawing was not touched.

drawing.description: The P&ID to read (DXF; a DWG only on a live seat).

instrument_csv.description: Where to write the instrument index CSV.

line_csv.description: Where to write the line list CSV.

equipment_csv.description: Where to write the equipment list CSV.

tolerance.description: Snap distance in drawing units within which a line end meets a port.

steps.purpose: Record the document's content revision before anything reads it.
Read the connectivity graph: nodes with their source and confidence, edges, dangling ends.
steps.evidence: nodes, edges, dangling, unclassified, and stats.confidence_min.

steps.purpose: The instrument index: tag, ISA-5.1 function and loop, what each is connected to.
steps.evidence: rows with tag, func, loop, description and confidence; the CSV at csv_path.

steps.purpose: The line list: every line with what it runs from and to.
steps.evidence: rows with line number (when drawn), from/to tag and port, length; the CSV at csv_path.

steps.purpose: The equipment list: tags, kinds, ports and connections.
steps.evidence: rows with tag, kind, ports, connected lines and confidence; the CSV at csv_path.

steps.purpose: Record the revision after the reads.
steps.evidence: The same document_id and revision as before.

postconditions.says: The graph read the drawing's entities.
The lowest node confidence is stated, so a reader knows how far to trust the lists.
The instrument index is on disk.
The line list is on disk.
The equipment list is on disk.
At least one line was read.
The lists were read from the document that was opened.
Reading the lists did not modify the drawing.
